title: team-2005-merritt-trophy
label: Karl Brown

won.source: The fed's own tournament final broadcast, posted the same day: Brown beat Victor Molotov with the Dragon's Bite, following a Dragonrana, at Madison Square Garden.

how: Won the TEAM Invitational Tournament final, beating five opponents from five different first-round pairings across the whole bracket.
note: No further tournament or Chad Merritt Trophy defense is recorded in the era's own record; the census lane's own era map records the trophy's own continuation into later, unread eras of this wing.

title: team-2005-championship-of-champions
label: D!

won.source: A repost of the fed's own full Tournament of Champions broadcast, found: D! beats Mr. Amazing! in the final, snapping Amazing's own protective mask into his face before a top-rope elbow drop.

lost.source: The 2006 Dupree Cup Finals broadcast: D! is announced stripped of the title after being fired by New Alberta Professional Wrestling for backstage conduct.

note: Successfully defended against Karl Brown at SuperShow I (22 July 2006) before Mr. Amazing! attacked him after the bell; declared vacant at the Finals, with a vacant-title match against Jake Hix set for SuperShow II, outside this era's own window.

note: The first-ever TEAM FREE FOR ALL~! Championship.

won.source: SuperShow IV's own five-way battle royal broadcast.

lost.source: SuperShow VI: Munson Monsoon eliminates Douglas.

won.source: SuperShow VI's own battle royal broadcast.

title: team-2005-challenge-championship
label: Ravager

won.source: SuperShow III's own three-way steel cage broadcast: Ravager escapes the cage after a top-rope brainbuster on Nova, becoming the first-ever champion.

note: Successfully defended in a points-scored charity match against Rob Franklin (SuperShow V), a falls-count-anywhere match against the Canadian Loonie and Professor Tremendous (SuperShow VI), and against Professor Tremendous again at SuperShow VII (result-only, no match text survives); a lumberjack defense against Shawn Hart (SuperShow IV) is recorded result-only, its own match text never written up. Ravager did not defend the title in the 2008 TEAM Invitational Tournament window, instead advancing to that tournament's Final Four; a defense against Fusenshoff was announced afterward with no stipulation yet set.

lost.source: TEAM SuperShow XI's own broadcast (posted 2009-10-08, of a show whose own RP deadline was 24 August 2009): Olvir Arsvinnar wins a dog collar match, ending Ravager's own Challenge Championship reign "since its inception."
